stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD. Anvi measures $\angle A = \angle B = \angle C = \angle D = 90^\circ$.

Can she classify ABCD as a rectangle without separately checking that opposite sides are equal?

options.text: Yes: a quadrilateral with all angles $90^\circ$ is a rectangle; opposite-side equalities then follow.
She should call the figure a right angle, not a rectangle.
Yes, even if A, B, C, D were only three rays and not a closed quadrilateral.
The same rule also classifies any open broken line of four right turns as a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: All four angles 90° in a quadrilateral make a rectangle; opposite sides follow. Renaming it a right angle swaps the class. Dropping the closed-quadrilateral condition, or extending the rule to open polylines, breaks the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as rectangle ABCD with four right-angle marks.
